# Task 5.7 - Referral & Trust Information Visibility in Dashboards

## Overview
This document defines visibility and signal policy for referral and trust information in dashboards, without implementing referral logic or trust calculation. This is a **policy and architecture document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. It ensures referral and trust data are displayed appropriately based on role and visibility rules.

---

## ?? CRITICAL RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

**This task is VISIBILITY & SIGNAL POLICY ONLY.**

? **NO referral logic**  
? **NO trust calculation**  
? **NO backend enforcement**  
? **NO dashboards UI**  
? **NO moderation actions**  
? **NO data mutation**

If any code is written, it must be rejected immediately.

---

## ?? PURPOSE (Senior Architect View)

This task exists to define visibility and signal policy for referral and trust information in dashboards, without implementing referral logic or trust calculation.

It ensures:
- Referral and trust data are displayed appropriately
- Visibility rules from Module 3 are respected
- Dashboard displays signals, doesn't compute them
- Cursor AI does not invent referral or trust logic

This task answers:
**"What referral and trust information can each role see in dashboards - and what must remain hidden?"**

---

## ?? REFERRAL & TRUST VISIBILITY IN DASHBOARDS

### ?? Pandit Dashboard (Own Data Only)

**Referral Information:**
- **Own referral links summary**
  - Number of referral links generated
  - Active vs inactive referral links
  - Referral link usage counts
  - Data from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

- **Referred Pandits summary**
  - Count of Pandits referred
  - Referred Pandits' status (active/pending/rejected)
  - Referral chain depth (own level only)
  - Data from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

- **Referred-by indicator** (if visible per Task 3.7 rules)
  - Who referred this Pandit
  - Only shown if visible per Task 3.7 visibility rules
  - Subject to Module 3 visibility rules
  - Data from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

**Trust Information:**
- **Own trust indicators**
  - Trust badges earned
  - Trust chain depth (own position)
  - Trust health indicators (own only)
  - Data from Module 10 (Public Trust Display)

- **Referral eligibility signal** (read-only)
  - Can generate referral links (yes/no)
  - Eligibility status indicator
  - Signal from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

**?? Important Notes:**
- **Subject to Task 3.7 visibility rules**
  - Referral visibility controlled by Module 3
  - Trust visibility controlled by Module 10
  - Dashboard respects visibility rules

- **Read-only information**
  - Pandit cannot edit referral data
  - Pandit cannot modify trust scores
  - Dashboard displays, doesn't compute

---

### ?? Admin Pandit Dashboard (Summary Only)

**Referral Information:**
- **System-wide referral summaries**
  - Total referral links generated
  - Active referral link count
  - Referral usage statistics
  - Data from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

- **Trust chain health indicators**
  - Overall trust chain integrity
  - Trust chain depth distribution
  - Trust chain anomaly flags
  - Data from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

- **Referral abuse flags** (summary)
  - Potential referral abuse indicators
  - Anomaly detection flags
  - Escalation-worthy referral issues
  - Data from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

**Trust Information:**
- **Trust ecosystem health**
  - Overall trust health metrics
  - Trust distribution summaries
  - Trust anomaly detection
  - Data from Module 10 (Public Trust Display)

- **Trust-related alerts**
  - Trust manipulation flags
  - Trust abuse indicators
  - Trust policy violations
  - Data from Module 10 (Public Trust Display)

**?? Important Notes:**
- **Summary data only**
  - Aggregated statistics, not individual details
  - High-level indicators, not granular data
  - Overview for monitoring purposes

- **No individual referral details**
  - Admin Pandit sees summaries, not individual referrals
  - No deep-dive into specific referral chains
  - Summary-level oversight only

---

### ?? Super Admin Dashboard (Full Visibility)

**Referral Information:**
- **Complete referral system overview**
  - All referral links (active and inactive)
  - Complete referral chain visibility
  - Referral usage statistics (all)
  - Data from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

  - Complete trust chain visibility
  - Trust chain depth analysis
  - Trust chain anomaly detection
  - Data from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

  - Complete anomaly detection
  - Referral manipulation indicators
  - Data from Module 3 (Referral & Trust Chain)

**Trust Information:**
- **Complete trust ecosystem**
  - All trust indicators and scores
  - Complete trust chain visibility
  - Trust distribution analysis
  - Data from Module 10 (Public Trust Display)

- **Trust governance overview**
  - Trust policy compliance
  - Trust abuse detection
  - Trust manipulation flags
  - Data from Module 10 (Public Trust Display) and Module 11 (Governance)

**?? Important Notes:**
- **Full system visibility**
  - Super Admin sees all referral and trust data
  - Complete system-wide oversight
  - No filtering or restrictions

- **Oversight and monitoring**
  - System-wide referral health
  - Trust ecosystem monitoring
  - Abuse detection and alerts

---

## ?? HARD BOUNDARIES (LOCKED)

**Referral & Trust Information in Dashboards must NEVER:**

1. **Compute trust scores**
   - Trust calculation belongs to Module 10
   - Dashboard displays trust indicators, doesn't compute them
   - Trust data is read-only

2. **Generate referral links**
   - Referral generation belongs to Module 3
   - Dashboard shows referral summaries, doesn't generate
   - Referral generation happens in Module 3

3. **Modify referral or trust data**
   - Referral and trust data are read-only
   - Dashboard displays, doesn't mutate
   - Data mutations belong to respective modules

4. **Bypass Task 3.7 visibility rules**
   - Visibility rules from Module 3 must be respected
   - Dashboard displays based on visibility rules
   - No bypassing of visibility restrictions

5. **Show hidden referral information**
   - Hidden referral data stays hidden
   - Visibility rules are enforced
   - Privacy and security maintained

---

### ?? Dashboard Referral & Trust Visibility DEPENDS ON:

1. **Module 3 - Referral & Trust Chain**
   - Provides referral summaries
   - Provides trust chain information
   - Provides visibility rules (Task 3.7)
   - Provides referral eligibility signals

2. **Module 10 - Public Trust Display**
   - Provides trust indicators
   - Provides trust badges
   - Provides trust health metrics

3. **Module 11 - Governance**
   - Provides visibility overrides
   - Controls referral/trust visibility based on moderation
   - Enforces governance decisions

### ?? Dashboard Referral & Trust Visibility is CONSUMED BY:

- **Dashboard users (Pandit, Admin Pandit, Super Admin)**
  - Dashboards display referral and trust information
  - Not consumed by other backend modules
  - Human operator interface only

**Dashboards display referral and trust signals - they do not compute or modify them.**

## ?? VISIBILITY RULES FROM MODULE 3 (Task 3.7)

### Task 3.7 Visibility Rules Applied:

1. **Referred-by visibility**
   - Fully blocked referrer ? ? Not visible
   - Limited blocked referrer ? ?? Visible with warning flag
   - Active referrer ? ? Normal visibility

2. **Trust chain visibility**
   - Trust chain depth visibility
   - Trust chain integrity indicators
   - Trust chain anomaly flags

3. **Referral eligibility**
   - Eligibility based on referrer status
   - Eligibility based on moderation state
   - Eligibility signals displayed

**?? Dashboard respects all Module 3 visibility rules.**

### Architectural Reasons:

1. **Respect Module 3 Visibility Rules**
   - Task 3.7 defines visibility rules
   - Dashboard must respect these rules
   - No bypassing of visibility restrictions

2. **Protect Privacy and Security**
   - Referral and trust data can be sensitive
   - Visibility rules protect privacy
   - Security boundaries maintained

3. **Clear Display Boundaries**
   - Define what each role can see
   - No accidental data exposure
   - Clear visibility patterns

4. **Module Ownership Respected**
   - Referral data belongs to Module 3
   - Trust data belongs to Module 10
   - Dashboard displays, doesn't own

5. **Future Flexibility**

   - Dashboard display can change
   - Policy remains stable

### Practical Benefits:

- Task 3.7 rules are authoritative
- Dashboard displays based on visibility rules
- No bypassing of restrictions

### 2. Read-Only Display
- Referral and trust data are read-only
- Dashboard displays, doesn't compute

- Each role sees appropriate information

It ensures reviews remain owned and controlled by Module 9, with dashboards surfacing signals and summaries only.

## ?? CRITICAL RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

- Reviews remain owned and controlled by Module 9

# Task 5.9 - Media Visibility, Reporting & Approval Signals in Dashboards

## Overview
This document defines how media-related information is surfaced in dashboards, without allowing dashboards to approve, reject, upload, or remove media. This is a **policy and architecture document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. It ensures media approval remains policy-driven and event-based, with dashboards exposing status, counts, and alerts only.

---

## ?? CRITICAL RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

**This task is MEDIA STATUS, VISIBILITY & SIGNAL POLICY ONLY.**

? **NO media upload logic**  
? **NO media storage logic**  
? **NO media approval execution**  
? **NO media rejection execution**  
? **NO backend enforcement**  
? **NO dashboards UI**  
? **NO data mutation**

If any code is written, it must be rejected immediately.

---

## ?? PURPOSE (Senior Architect View)

This task exists to define how media-related information is surfaced in dashboards, without allowing dashboards to approve, reject, upload, or remove media.

It ensures:
- Media approval remains policy-driven and event-based
- Dashboards expose status, counts, and alerts only
- Governance workflows remain the sole execution path
- Cursor AI does not turn dashboards into moderation tools

# Task 5.10 - Profile Completion Metrics, Signals & Dashboard Nudges

## Overview
This document defines how profile completion metrics are exposed and communicated in dashboards, without allowing those metrics to influence system behavior. This is a **policy and architecture document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. It ensures completion metrics are descriptive, not authoritative, and dashboards guide Pandits with nudges, not penalties.

---

## ?? CRITICAL RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

**This task is METRICS DISPLAY, SIGNALS & NUDGING POLICY ONLY.**

? **NO calculation logic**  
? **NO enforcement or blocking**  
? **NO ranking or scoring logic**  
? **NO search / SEO coupling**  
? **NO dashboards UI**  
? **NO backend validation**

If any code is written, it must be rejected immediately.

---

## ?? PURPOSE (Senior Architect View)

This task exists to define how profile completion metrics are exposed and communicated in dashboards, without allowing those metrics to influence system behavior.

It ensures:
- Completion metrics are descriptive, not authoritative
- Dashboards guide Pandits with nudges, not penalties
- No coupling with Search, SEO, Trust, or Governance
- Cursor AI does not convert metrics into enforcement rules

This task answers:
**"How does the system display profile readiness and guide users - without affecting visibility, ranking, or permissions?"**

---

## ?? PROFILE COMPLETION METRICS - DEFINITION (LOCKED)

### Profile Completion Representation:

**Completion Percentage (0-100)**
- Calculated percentage of profile completion
- Based on mandatory fields from Task 4.6
- Displayed as a number, not a gatekeeper
- Data from Module 4 (Pandit Profile)

**Completion State**
- **Complete** - All mandatory fields filled
- **Incomplete** - Some mandatory fields missing
- State is descriptive, not authoritative
- Data from Module 4 (Pandit Profile)

**Missing Sections List (high-level only)**
- List of sections that need completion
- High-level guidance only
- Not detailed field-by-field breakdown
- Data from Module 4 (Pandit Profile)

**?? Metrics are:**
- ? Displayed in dashboards
- ? Used for guidance and nudges
- ? NOT used for search ranking
- ? NOT used for SEO visibility
- ? NOT used for trust calculation
- ? NOT used for governance decisions

### 1. Passive Display Only
- Dashboards display notifications
- They do not generate or send notifications
- Notification logic is external

### 2. Informational Signals
- Notifications are informational

- Super Admin sees all alerts

- Dashboard displays, doesn't act

- Notification delivery is centralized
- Dashboard displays, doesn't deliver
- Delivery system is separate

- **"Alert display" ? notification generation**
  - Display is read-only
  - Generation belongs to respective modules
  - No coupling between them

- **"Alert visibility" ? alert delivery**
  - Visibility is display-only
  - Delivery belongs to notification module
  - No coupling between them

- **"Alert summary" ? alert action**
  - Summary is informational
  - Actions belong to respective modules
  - No action execution from alerts

- **"Notification signal" ? notification command**
  - Signal is informational
  - Command would be enforcement
  - No enforcement from notifications

**These distinctions prevent misuse.**

# Task 6.1 - Availability Strategy & Scope Boundaries Summary

## Overview
Successfully locked the meaning, ownership, and limits of Availability before any implementation begins. This is a **strategy and boundaries document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. The document ensures availability is a signal, not a commitment, and Pandits control availability, not the system.

**NO CODE** - Strategy & Boundaries Only

- Define what availability represents conceptually
- Define what availability is responsible for
- Define what availability must never do

- Define which modules consume availability signals

---

## Key Definitions

### Availability - Conceptual Definition (LOCKED)

**Availability Represents:**
- Pandit-declared time windows
- An intent to be available
- A planning and discovery signal

**Availability Is:**
- Calendar-based
- Day-wise & time-slot oriented
- Contextual (pooja, city, area)
- Editable by Pandit
- Read-only for consumers

**Availability Is NOT:**
- ? A booking
- ? A reservation
- ? A guarantee
- ? A lead
- ? A conversion
- ? A payment trigger

---

## What Availability Is Responsible For

**Availability WILL:**
1. Allow Pandits to define when they are available
2. Support day-wise and time-slot definitions
3. Support pooja-specific availability
4. Support city & local-area context
5. Emit read-only signals to:
   - Search & filters (Module 7)
   - Dashboards (Module 5)
   - Recommendation systems (future)
6. Support conceptual auditability (change awareness)

---

## What Availability Must Never Do

**Availability MUST NEVER:**
1. Accept requests
2. Confirm dates
3. Lock time slots
4. Reject users
5. Handle payments
6. Influence SEO or trust
7. Act as a KPI or score
8. Track or score leads
9. Trigger notifications

|---------|-------|
| Availability definition | Pandit |
| Availability editing | Pandit only |
| Availability storage | Module 6 |
| Availability consumption | Other modules (read-only) |
| Booking decisions | ? Not here (Module 8) |
| Lead tracking | ? Not here (Separate module) |

**Key Ownership Rules:**
- Pandit owns availability definition
- Module 6 owns availability storage
- Other modules consume (read-only)
- Booking decisions are separate

## Module Dependencies

### Availability DEPENDS ON:
- Module 1 - Auth (Pandit identity)
- Module 2 - Approved cities, areas, poojas
- Module 4 - Pandit profile (context only)

### Availability is CONSUMED BY:
- Module 5 - Dashboards (display only)
- Module 7 - Search & filters
- Recommendation engine (future, read-only)

---

## Key Architectural Principles

1. **Signal, Not Commitment** - Availability is a signal
2. **Pandit Control** - Pandits control availability
3. **Read-Only Consumption** - Other modules consume read-only
4. **No State Mutation** - Availability never mutates system state
5. **Clear Separation** - Availability is separate from booking/payments/leads

# Task 6.1 - Availability Strategy & Scope Boundaries

## Overview
This document locks the meaning, ownership, and limits of Availability before any implementation begins. This is a **strategy and boundaries document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. It ensures availability is a signal, not a commitment, and Pandits control availability, not the system.

---

## ?? CRITICAL RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

**This task is STRATEGY & BOUNDARIES ONLY.**

? **NO Django models**  
? **NO migrations**  
? **NO backend logic**  
? **NO frontend UI**  
? **NO dashboards logic**  
? **NO booking workflows**  
? **NO payment logic**  
? **NO analytics / KPI tracking**  
? **NO notifications**

If any code appears ? REJECT IMMEDIATELY.

---

## ?? PURPOSE (Senior Architect View)

This task exists to lock the meaning, ownership, and limits of Availability before any implementation begins.

It ensures:
- Availability is a signal, not a commitment
- Pandits control availability, not the system
- "Check Availability" remains read-only
- Availability never mutates system state
- Booking, payments, and leads remain out of scope
- Cursor AI cannot confuse availability with booking or enforcement

This task answers:
**"What does Availability represent in this platform - and what must it NEVER do?"**

---

## ?? AVAILABILITY - CONCEPTUAL DEFINITION (LOCKED)

### Availability Represents:

**Pandit-Declared Time Windows**
- Pandits declare when they are available
- Self-declared intent, not system-enforced commitment
- Editable by Pandit at any time

**An Intent to Be Available**
- Availability expresses willingness
- Not a guarantee or reservation
- Subject to change by Pandit

**A Planning and Discovery Signal**
- Used for search and filtering
- Used for discovery by users
- Informational only, not transactional

### Availability Is:

- **Calendar-based**
  - Organized by days and dates
  - Calendar-oriented mental model

- **Day-wise & time-slot oriented**
  - Defined per day
  - Time ranges within days
  - Supports recurring patterns

- **Contextual (pooja, city, area)**
  - May be specific to pooja types
  - May be specific to cities/areas
  - Contextual filtering support

- **Editable by Pandit**
  - Pandit has full control
  - Can add, edit, or remove availability
  - No system enforcement

- **Read-only for consumers**
  - Users can view availability
  - Users cannot modify availability
  - Read-only signal consumption

### Availability Is NOT:

? **A booking**
- Availability is not a booking
- Booking is separate (Module 8)
- No booking logic in availability

? **A reservation**
- Availability is not a reservation
- No slot locking or reservation system
- No commitment implied

? **A guarantee**
- Availability is not a guarantee
- No enforcement of availability
- Subject to change

? **A lead**
- Availability is not a lead
- Lead tracking is separate
- No lead conversion logic

? **A conversion**
- Availability is not a conversion metric
- No conversion tracking
- No KPI calculation

? **A payment trigger**
- Availability is not a payment trigger
- Payment logic is separate
- No payment integration

---

## ?? WHAT AVAILABILITY IS RESPONSIBLE FOR

### Availability WILL:

1. **Allow Pandits to define when they are available**
   - Pandits can declare availability windows
   - Full control over availability definition
   - No system interference

2. **Support day-wise and time-slot definitions**
   - Day-based availability (e.g., Monday-Friday)
   - Time-slot ranges (e.g., 9 AM - 5 PM)
   - Recurring patterns support

3. **Support pooja-specific availability**
   - Availability may vary by pooja type
   - Different availability for different poojas
   - Pooja context support

4. **Support city & local-area context**
   - Availability may vary by location
   - City-level availability
   - Local area-level availability (optional)

5. **Emit read-only signals to:**
   - **Search & filters (Module 7)**
     - Availability used for search filtering
     - Read-only consumption
     - No mutation of availability

   - **Dashboards (Module 5)**
     - Availability displayed in dashboards
     - Read-only display
     - No editing via dashboards

   - **Recommendation systems (future)**
     - Availability used for recommendations
     - Read-only consumption
     - No mutation of availability

6. **Support conceptual auditability (change awareness)**
   - Track when availability changes
   - Audit trail for availability updates
   - Change history support

---

## ?? WHAT AVAILABILITY MUST NEVER DO

### Availability MUST NEVER:

? **Accept requests**
- Availability does not accept booking requests
- Request handling belongs to Module 8
- No request processing logic

? **Confirm dates**
- Availability does not confirm dates
- Confirmation belongs to Module 8
- No confirmation logic

? **Lock time slots**
- Availability does not lock time slots
- Slot locking belongs to Module 8
- No locking mechanism

? **Reject users**
- Availability does not reject users
- Rejection belongs to Module 8
- No rejection logic

? **Handle payments**
- Availability does not handle payments
- Payment logic is separate
- No payment integration

? **Influence SEO or trust**
- Availability does not affect SEO
- Availability does not affect trust
- No coupling with SEO or trust modules

? **Act as a KPI or score**
- Availability is not a KPI
- Availability is not a score
- No metrics calculation

? **Track or score leads**
- Availability does not track leads
- Availability does not score leads
- Lead tracking is separate

? **Trigger notifications**
- Availability does not trigger notifications
- Notification logic is separate
- No notification integration

---

## ?? OWNERSHIP & AUTHORITY (LOCKED)

| Concern | Owner |
|---------|-------|
| **Availability definition** | Pandit |
| **Availability editing** | Pandit only |
| **Availability storage** | Module 6 |
| **Availability consumption** | Other modules (read-only) |
| **Booking decisions** | ? Not here (Module 8) |
| **Lead tracking** | ? Not here (Separate module) |

### Key Ownership Rules:

1. **Pandit Owns Availability Definition**
   - Only Pandits can define availability
   - Admin Pandit cannot edit
   - Super Admin cannot edit
   - System cannot auto-modify

2. **Module 6 Owns Availability Storage**
   - Availability data stored in Module 6
   - No duplication in other modules
   - Centralized storage

3. **Other Modules Consume (Read-Only)**
   - Search & filters consume availability
   - Dashboards consume availability
   - Recommendation systems consume availability
   - All consumption is read-only

4. **Booking Decisions Are Separate**
   - Booking decisions belong to Module 8
   - Availability does not make booking decisions
   - Clear separation maintained

---

## ?? EXPLICIT MODULE DEPENDENCIES

### ?? Availability DEPENDS ON:

1. **Module 1 - Auth (Pandit identity)**
   - Provides Pandit user identity
   - Authentication and authorization
   - Role-based access control

2. **Module 2 - Approved cities, areas, poojas**
   - Provides master data for cities
   - Provides master data for local areas
   - Provides master data for poojas
   - Only approved master data used

3. **Module 4 - Pandit profile (context only)**
   - Provides profile context
   - Links availability to profile
   - No availability logic in profile

### ?? Availability is CONSUMED BY:

1. **Module 5 - Dashboards (display only)**
   - Dashboards display availability
   - Read-only consumption
   - No editing via dashboards

2. **Module 7 - Search & filters**
   - Search uses availability for filtering
   - Read-only consumption
   - No mutation of availability

3. **Recommendation engine (future, read-only)**
   - Recommendations use availability
   - Read-only consumption
   - No mutation of availability

---

## ?? KEY ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES

### 1. Signal, Not Commitment
- Availability is a signal
- Not a commitment or guarantee
- Subject to change

### 2. Pandit Control
- Pandits control availability
- System does not enforce
- No system interference

### 3. Read-Only Consumption
- Other modules consume availability read-only
- No mutation of availability by consumers
- Clear consumption boundaries

### 4. No State Mutation
- Availability never mutates system state
- No booking or confirmation logic
- No payment or lead tracking

### 5. Clear Separation
- Availability is separate from booking
- Availability is separate from payments
- Availability is separate from leads

# Task 6.2 - Availability Data Model & Ownership Rules Summary

## Overview
Successfully created the Availability data model following the minimal, extensible design that is booking-agnostic, payment-agnostic, and KPI-agnostic. This is a **MODELS ONLY** task - no views, serializers, APIs, or business logic.

---

## Task Type
**MODELS ONLY** - Data Structure Only

---

## Changes Made

### 1. Created Availability App
- **Command:** python manage.py startapp availability
- **Location:** availability/ directory at project root
- **Status:** App created with default Django structure

### 2. Created Availability Model
**File:** availability/models.py

**Model Details:**
- **Model Name:** Availability
- **Ownership:** One Pandit ? Many Availability entries
- **Base Design:** Booking-agnostic, payment-agnostic, KPI-agnostic

**Key Features:**

#### Ownership Field
- pandit (ForeignKey to User with role='pandit')
  - Links availability to Pandit
  - CASCADE on delete
  - Limited to Pandit role only

#### Temporal Fields
- day_of_week (IntegerField, choices, nullable)
  - For recurring availability (0=Monday, 6=Sunday)
  - Optional if using specific_date
  
- specific_date (DateField, nullable)
  - For one-off availability
  - Optional if using day_of_week
  
- start_time (TimeField, required)
  - Start time of availability window
  
- end_time (TimeField, required)
  - End time of availability window
  
- is_recurring (BooleanField, default=True)
  - Indicates if recurring (day_of_week) or one-off (specific_date)

#### Contextual Fields (from Module 2 - Master Data)
- city (ForeignKey to City, required)
  - City where availability applies
  - PROTECT on delete (master data protection)
  
- area (ForeignKey to LocalArea, optional)
  - Local area where availability applies
  - PROTECT on delete
  
- pooja (ForeignKey to Pooja, optional)
  - Pooja type for which availability applies
  - PROTECT on delete

#### State Fields (Descriptive Only)
- is_active (BooleanField, default=True)
  - Descriptive only, does not enforce availability
  
- created_at (DateTimeField, auto_now_add)
  - Creation timestamp
  
- updated_at (DateTimeField, auto_now)
  - Last update timestamp

### 3. Model Validation
- **clean() method:**
  - Ensures either day_of_week OR specific_date is set, not both
  - Validates time range (end_time > start_time)
  
- **save() override:**
  - Calls full_clean() to enforce validation

### 4. Model Meta Configuration
- **Database table:** availability_availability
- **Ordering:** By pandit, day_of_week/specific_date, start_time
- **Indexes:**
  - ['pandit', 'is_active'] - For filtering by Pandit
  - ['city', 'is_active'] - For filtering by city
  - ['day_of_week', 'is_active'] - For recurring availability queries
  - ['specific_date', 'is_active'] - For date-specific queries

### 5. Updated Settings
**File:** nityadharma/settings/base.py

**Changes:**
- Added 'availability' to INSTALLED_APPS

**Before:**

python
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # ... Django apps ...
    'core',
    'accounts',
    'referrals',
    'masterdata',
    'profiles',
]


**After:**

python
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # ... Django apps ...
    'core',
    'accounts',
    'referrals',
    'masterdata',
    'profiles',
    'availability',
]


---

## Core Ownership Rule (LOCKED)

? **One Pandit ? Many Availability entries**
- A Pandit can have multiple availability entries
- Each entry represents a time window

? **Availability belongs exclusively to Pandit**
- No user/customer references
- No booking references
- Pandit-only ownership

? **Availability does NOT belong to users, leads, or bookings**
- No foreign keys to users (except Pandit)
- No foreign keys to bookings
- No lead tracking fields

---

- No booking status fields

- No customer tracking

---

- No duplication of master data

- Single source of truth

? **No denormalized analytics**
- No cached counts
- No aggregated metrics
- Pure normalized structure

---

## Model Relationships

### Foreign Keys (Outgoing)
- pandit ? accounts.User (CASCADE)
- city ? masterdata.City (PROTECT)
- area ? masterdata.LocalArea (PROTECT, optional)
- pooja ? masterdata.Pooja (PROTECT, optional)

### Reverse Relations (Incoming)
- User.availabilities ? Many Availability entries
- City.availabilities ? Many Availability entries
- LocalArea.availabilities ? Many Availability entries
- Pooja.availabilities ? Many Availability entries

# Task 6.2 - Availability Data Model & Ownership Rules Summary

## Overview
Successfully created the Availability data model following the minimal, extensible design that is booking-agnostic, payment-agnostic, and KPI-agnostic. This is a **MODELS ONLY** task - no views, serializers, APIs, or business logic.

---

## Task Type
**MODELS ONLY** - Data Structure Only

---

## Changes Made

### 1. Created Availability App
- **Command:** python manage.py startapp availability
- **Location:** availability/ directory at project root
- **Status:** App created with default Django structure

### 2. Created Availability Model
**File:** availability/models.py

**Model Details:**
- **Model Name:** Availability
- **Ownership:** One Pandit ? Many Availability entries
- **Base Design:** Booking-agnostic, payment-agnostic, KPI-agnostic

**Key Features:**

#### Ownership Field
- pandit (ForeignKey to User)
  - Links availability to Pandit
  - CASCADE on delete
  - **NOTE:** Role enforcement (role="pandit") is handled at service/permission layer, not at database level. This ForeignKey does not enforce role constraints.

#### Temporal Fields
- day_of_week (IntegerField, choices, nullable)
  - For recurring availability (0=Monday, 6=Sunday)
  - Optional if using specific_date
  
- specific_date (DateField, nullable)
  - For one-off availability
  - Optional if using day_of_week
  
- start_time (TimeField, required)
  - Start time of availability window
  
- end_time (TimeField, required)
  - End time of availability window
  
- is_recurring (BooleanField, default=True)
  - Descriptive field: True if using day_of_week (recurring), False if using specific_date (one-off)
  - This is descriptive only and may be derived in future refactoring

#### Contextual Fields (from Module 2 - Master Data)
- city (ForeignKey to City, required)
  - City where availability applies
  - PROTECT on delete (master data protection)
  
- area (ForeignKey to LocalArea, optional)
  - Local area where availability applies
  - PROTECT on delete
  
- pooja (ForeignKey to Pooja, optional)
  - Pooja type for which availability applies
  - PROTECT on delete

#### State Fields (Descriptive Only)
- is_active (BooleanField, default=True)
  - Descriptive only, does not enforce availability
  
- created_at (DateTimeField, auto_now_add)
  - Creation timestamp
  
- updated_at (DateTimeField, auto_now)
  - Last update timestamp

### 3. Model Validation
- **clean() method:**
  - Provided for Django admin and forms only
  - NOT runtime enforcement logic
  - Ensures either day_of_week OR specific_date is set, not both
  - Validates time range (end_time > start_time)
  - Actual validation enforcement happens at service/permission layer (Task 6.3+)
  
- **No save() override:**
  - MODELS ONLY principle: no enforcement logic in model
  - Validation enforcement deferred to service layer

### 4. Model Meta Configuration
- **Database table:** availability_availability
- **Ordering:** By pandit, day_of_week/specific_date, start_time
- **Indexes:**
  - ['pandit', 'is_active'] - For filtering by Pandit
  - ['city', 'is_active'] - For filtering by city
  - ['day_of_week', 'is_active'] - For recurring availability queries
  - ['specific_date', 'is_active'] - For date-specific queries

### 5. Updated Settings
**File:** nityadharma/settings/base.py

**Changes:**
- Added 'availability' to INSTALLED_APPS

**After:**

# Task 6.3 - Pandit Availability Input Rules (Calendar-Based)

## Overview
This document defines how Pandits are allowed to INPUT availability, conceptually, using a calendar-based mental model, without implementing UI or logic. This is a **policy and architecture document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. It ensures Pandits understand availability as self-declared intent, input remains simple and editable, and no confusion with bookings or confirmations.

---

## ?? CRITICAL RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

**This task is INPUT RULES & POLICY ONLY.**

? **NO UI wireframes**  
? **NO calendar components**  
? **NO backend logic**  
? **NO validation code**  
? **NO booking workflows**  
? **NO payments**  
? **NO analytics / KPI logic**

If any code appears ? REJECT IMMEDIATELY.

---

## ?? PURPOSE (Senior Architect View)

This task exists to define how Pandits are allowed to INPUT availability, conceptually, using a calendar-based mental model, without implementing UI or logic.

It ensures:
- Pandits understand availability as self-declared intent
- Input remains simple, predictable, and editable
- No confusion with bookings or confirmations
- Cursor AI does not design booking-like flows

This task answers:
**"How does a Pandit express availability in the system - conceptually?"**

---

## ?? CALENDAR-BASED INPUT - CONCEPTUAL RULES (LOCKED)

### Pandit Availability Input Is:

**Calendar-Oriented (Days, Not Bookings)**
- Availability is organized by calendar days
- Days are the primary unit of input
- Not organized by bookings or reservations

**Declarative ("I Am Available"), Not Transactional**
- Pandit declares availability
- Not a transaction or commitment
- Simple statement of intent

**Editable at Any Time**
- Pandit can modify availability anytime
- No restrictions on when changes can be made
- No approval required

**Overridable by Pandit**
- Pandit has full control
- Can override any previous availability
- No system interference

### Pandits May Define Availability Using:

**Days of the Week (Recurring)**
- Monday through Sunday
- Recurring weekly pattern
- Example: "Available every Monday"

**Specific Dates (One-Off)**
- Specific calendar dates
- One-time availability
- Example: "Available on 2024-12-25"

**Time Ranges Within a Day**
- Start time and end time
- Multiple time ranges per day allowed
- Example: "9:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 2:00 PM - 5:00 PM"

**?? Input represents willingness, not commitment.**

---

## ?? ALLOWED INPUT ACTIONS (CONCEPTUAL)

### Pandit MAY:

1. **Mark days as available / unavailable**
   - Can mark any day as available
   - Can mark any day as unavailable
   - Full control over day-level availability

2. **Define time ranges for a day**
   - Can specify start and end times
   - Can define multiple time ranges per day
   - Can leave entire day available (all day)

3. **Add recurring availability (e.g., every Monday)**
   - Can set up weekly recurring patterns
   - Can specify which days of week
   - Can combine multiple recurring days

4. **Add date-specific overrides (e.g., festival days)**
   - Can override recurring patterns for specific dates
   - Can add one-off availability for special dates
   - Specific dates take precedence over recurring patterns

5. **Edit or remove availability entries at any time**
   - Can edit any existing availability entry
   - Can delete any availability entry
   - No restrictions on editing or deletion

**?? All input actions are voluntary and fully controlled by Pandit.**

---

## ?? DISALLOWED INPUT BEHAVIOR

### Pandit MUST NOT:

? **Accept bookings**
- Availability input is not booking acceptance
- Booking acceptance belongs to Module 8
- No booking logic in availability input

? **Confirm users**
- Availability input is not user confirmation
- User confirmation belongs to Module 8
- No confirmation logic in availability input

? **See demand or requests**
- Availability input does not show demand
- Demand/request viewing belongs to Module 8
- No demand tracking in availability input

? **Lock time slots**
- Availability input does not lock slots
- Slot locking belongs to Module 8
- No locking mechanism in availability input

? **Be forced to maintain availability**
- Availability input is fully voluntary
- No system enforcement of availability
- Pandit can have zero availability entries

**?? Availability input is fully voluntary - no enforcement or requirements.**

---

## ?? OWNERSHIP & EDIT RIGHTS (LOCKED)

### Availability Input Ownership:

**Availability input is Pandit-only**
- Only Pandits can input availability
- Regular users cannot input availability
- Admin Pandit cannot input availability for other Pandits

**Admin Pandit ? cannot edit**
- Admin Pandit cannot edit any Pandit's availability
- No override authority for availability
- Admin Pandit can only view (in dashboards)

**Super Admin ? cannot edit**
- Super Admin cannot edit any Pandit's availability
- No override authority for availability
- Super Admin can only view (in dashboards)

**System ? cannot auto-modify**
- System cannot automatically modify availability
- No system-generated availability
- No system enforcement of availability

**?? Only the Pandit who owns the availability can input or edit it.**

---

## ?? HARD BOUNDARIES (LOCKED)

### Calendar Input Must NOT:

? **Show bookings**
- Availability input does not display bookings
- Bookings belong to Module 8
- No booking information in availability input

? **Show user names**
- Availability input does not show user names
- User information belongs to Module 8
- No user data in availability input

? **Show conversion data**
- Availability input does not show conversion metrics
- Conversion tracking belongs to analytics module
- No KPI/metrics in availability input

? **Trigger notifications**
- Availability input does not trigger notifications
- Notification logic is separate
- No notification integration in availability input

? **Affect search ranking directly**
- Availability input does not affect search ranking
- Search ranking belongs to Module 7
- No ranking logic in availability input

**?? Availability input is pure input - no display, tracking, or enforcement logic.**

---

## ?? KEY CONCEPTUAL DISTINCTIONS

### Important Distinctions:

**"Availability Input" ? "Booking Acceptance"**
- Input is declaring availability
- Acceptance is confirming a booking
- These are separate concepts

**"Calendar View" ? "Booking Calendar"**
- Calendar view shows availability
- Booking calendar shows bookings
- These are separate views

**"Time Slot" ? "Booked Slot"**
- Time slot is available time
- Booked slot is reserved time
- These are separate states

**"Availability Entry" ? "Booking Request"**
- Entry is Pandit's declaration
- Request is user's inquiry
- These are separate entities

**These distinctions prevent confusion with booking workflows.**

---

## ?? WHY INPUT RULES ARE DEFINED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION

### Architectural Reasons:

1. **Prevent Booking Confusion**
   - Clear separation from booking logic
   - No booking-like flows in availability
   - Predictable input behavior

2. **Maintain Pandit Control**
   - Pandit has full control
   - No system interference
   - Clear ownership boundaries

3. **Simple and Predictable**
   - Input remains simple
   - No complex workflows
   - Easy to understand

4. **Future-Proof**
   - Input rules can evolve
   - UI can change
   - Policy remains stable

5. **Prevent Scope Creep**
   - Clear boundaries
   - No booking logic leakage
   - No payment logic leakage

### Practical Benefits:

- ? No booking confusion
- ? Pandit control maintained
- ? Simple and predictable
- ? Future-proof design
- ? Clear boundaries

---

## ?? INPUT PRINCIPLES

### 1. Calendar-Oriented Mental Model
- Availability is organized by calendar
- Days are primary unit
- Time ranges within days

### 2. Declarative, Not Transactional
- Pandit declares availability
- Not a transaction
- Simple statement of intent

### 3. Fully Editable
- Can edit anytime
- Can delete anytime
- No restrictions

### 4. Pandit-Only Control
- Only Pandit can input/edit
- No admin override
- No system auto-modification

### 5. No Booking Logic
- No booking acceptance
- No user confirmation
- No slot locking

## ?? DAY-WISE AVAILABILITY - CONCEPTUAL MODEL (LOCKED)

### Availability May Be Defined As:

**Weekly Recurring Days (e.g., Mon-Fri)**
- Days of the week that repeat weekly
- Example: Monday through Friday
- Recurring pattern

**Specific Calendar Dates (Exceptions)**
- Specific dates that override recurring patterns
- Example: December 25, 2024
- One-off availability

**Combination of Recurring + Override Rules**
- Base recurring pattern with specific date overrides
- Example: Available Monday-Friday, except December 25
- Specific dates override recurring patterns

**?? Specific dates override recurring patterns.**

---

## ?? TIME-SLOT DEFINITIONS (CONCEPTUAL)

### A Time Slot Represents:

**A Continuous Range of Time**
- Start time and end time
- Continuous time window
- Not discrete intervals

**Within a Single Day**
- Time slots are day-specific
- Each day can have multiple slots
- Slots do not span across days

### Examples:

**Morning Slot:**
- 6:00 AM - 10:00 AM
- Continuous 4-hour window

**Evening Slot:**
- 5:00 PM - 9:00 PM
- Continuous 4-hour window

### Time Slots:

**Are Not Discrete Bookings**
- Time slot is available time
- Not a booked reservation
- Not a confirmed appointment

**Do Not Imply Capacity**
- Time slot does not specify how many bookings
- No capacity limits in availability
- Capacity belongs to booking module

**Do Not Get Locked**
- Time slots are not locked
- No reservation mechanism
- No locking logic in availability

**?? Time slots are descriptive - they describe available time, not booked time.**

---

## ?? ALLOWED STRUCTURES

### Multiple Time Slots Per Day
- Pandit can define multiple time slots per day
- Example: Morning (9 AM - 12 PM) and Evening (5 PM - 8 PM)
- No limit on number of slots per day

### Gaps Between Slots
- Time slots can have gaps between them
- Example: 9 AM - 12 PM and 5 PM - 8 PM (gap from 12 PM - 5 PM)
- Gaps are allowed and normal

### Different Slots for Different Days
- Different days can have different time slots
- Example: Monday has 9 AM - 5 PM, Tuesday has 2 PM - 8 PM
- No requirement for consistency across days

**?? Flexibility in time slot structure - no rigid constraints.**

---

## ?? DISALLOWED STRUCTURES

### Overlapping Slots (Conceptually Discouraged)
- Overlapping time slots are conceptually discouraged
- Example: 9 AM - 12 PM and 11 AM - 2 PM (overlap from 11 AM - 12 PM)
- While technically possible, overlapping slots create ambiguity
- Should be avoided in practice

### Slot-Level Confirmations
- Time slots cannot be confirmed
- Confirmation belongs to booking module
- No confirmation logic in availability

### Slot-Based Pricing
- Time slots cannot have pricing
- Pricing belongs to payment module
- No pricing logic in availability

### Slot-Level KPIs
- Time slots cannot have KPIs
- KPI tracking belongs to analytics module
- No KPI logic in availability

**?? Time slots are descriptive only - no transactional or metric logic.**

---

## ?? HARD BOUNDARIES (LOCKED)

### Day-wise & Time-slot Definitions Must NEVER:

? **Act as Reservations**
- Time slots are not reservations
- Reservation logic belongs to Module 8
- No reservation mechanism

? **Enforce Attendance**
- Time slots do not enforce attendance
- Attendance tracking belongs to booking module
- No enforcement logic

? **Auto-Reject Users**
- Time slots do not reject users
- Rejection logic belongs to Module 8
- No rejection mechanism

? **Trigger Notifications**
- Time slots do not trigger notifications
- Notification logic is separate
- No notification integration

**?? Time slots are descriptive signals - they do not enforce, reject, or trigger actions.**

# Task 6.5 - Pooja-Specific Availability Rules Summary

## Overview
Successfully documented how availability may vary by pooja type, without turning availability into a booking or pricing system. This is a **policy and architecture document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. The document ensures Pandits can express capability-based availability, search can filter availability by pooja, and no pooja becomes a booking constraint.

---

## Task Type
**NO CODE** - Rules & Semantics Only

---

## Document Created

### File: POOJA_SPECIFIC_AVAILABILITY_RULES.md

**Purpose:**
- Define what pooja-specific availability represents
- Define how Pandits may associate availability with poojas
- Define what this availability must never imply
- Define how search may safely consume this signal
- Define hard boundaries that prevent booking or pricing logic

---

## Key Definitions

### Pooja-Specific Availability - Concept (LOCKED)

**Pooja-Specific Availability Means:**
- A Pandit may be available for certain poojas at certain times
- Availability reflects readiness, not acceptance

**?? Example (conceptual):**
- Morning: Available for Abhishekam
- Evening: Available for Gruha Pravesh
- (This is not a booking promise.)

**?? Availability reflects readiness, not acceptance.**

---

## Allowed Rules

**Pandit MAY:**
1. Associate availability entries with one or more poojas
2. Have different availability windows for different poojas
3. Update pooja availability anytime

**?? Pandits have full control over pooja-specific availability.**

---

## Disallowed Rules

**Pooja-Specific Availability MUST NOT:**
- ? Imply confirmation
- ? Enforce duration
- ? Attach pricing
- ? Reserve time slots
- ? Affect trust, SEO, or ranking

**?? Pooja availability is descriptive only - no transactional, pricing, or ranking logic.**

---

## Hard Boundaries (LOCKED)

**Pooja Availability Rules:**
- Pooja availability is advisory
- Final acceptance happens outside availability
- Search may filter, but not decide

**?? Pooja availability is advisory - acceptance and booking are separate.**

---

# Task 6.5 - Pooja-Specific Availability Rules

## Overview
This document defines how availability may vary by pooja type, without turning availability into a booking or pricing system. This is a **policy and architecture document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. It ensures Pandits can express capability-based availability, search can filter availability by pooja, and no pooja becomes a booking constraint.

---

## ?? CRITICAL RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

**This task is RULES & SEMANTICS ONLY.**

? **NO database changes**  
? **NO backend logic**  
? **NO pricing logic**  
? **NO booking or confirmation logic**  
? **NO dashboards UI**  
? **NO recommendation logic**

If any code or enforcement appears ? REJECT IMMEDIATELY.

---

## ?? PURPOSE (Senior Architect View)

This task exists to define how availability may vary by pooja type, without turning availability into a booking or pricing system.

It ensures:
- Pandits can express capability-based availability
- Search can filter availability by pooja
- No pooja becomes a booking constraint
- Cursor AI does not introduce demand or pricing logic

This task answers:
**"How does availability differ by pooja - conceptually and safely?"**

---

## ?? POOJA-SPECIFIC AVAILABILITY - CONCEPT (LOCKED)

### Pooja-Specific Availability Means:

**A Pandit May Be Available For:**
- Certain poojas
- At certain times
- Availability reflects readiness, not acceptance

**?? Example (conceptual):**
- Morning: Available for Abhishekam
- Evening: Available for Gruha Pravesh
- (This is not a booking promise.)

**?? Availability reflects readiness, not acceptance.**

---

## ?? ALLOWED RULES

### Pandit MAY:

1. **Associate availability entries with one or more poojas**
   - Can link availability to specific pooja types
   - Can have multiple poojas per availability entry
   - Can have different availability for different poojas

2. **Have different availability windows for different poojas**
   - Can specify different time slots for different poojas
   - Example: Morning for Pooja A, Evening for Pooja B
   - Flexible pooja-specific scheduling

3. **Update pooja availability anytime**
   - Can modify pooja associations anytime
   - Can add or remove pooja associations
   - No restrictions on updates

**?? Pandits have full control over pooja-specific availability.**

---

## ?? DISALLOWED RULES

### Pooja-Specific Availability MUST NOT:

? **Imply Confirmation**
- Pooja availability does not confirm bookings
- Confirmation belongs to Module 8
- No confirmation logic

? **Enforce Duration**
- Pooja availability does not enforce duration
- Duration belongs to booking module
- No duration enforcement

? **Attach Pricing**
- Pooja availability does not attach pricing
- Pricing belongs to payment module
- No pricing logic

? **Reserve Time Slots**
- Pooja availability does not reserve slots
- Reservation belongs to Module 8
- No reservation mechanism

? **Affect Trust, SEO, or Ranking**
- Pooja availability does not affect trust
- Pooja availability does not affect SEO
- Pooja availability does not affect ranking
- No coupling with other modules

**?? Pooja availability is descriptive only - no transactional, pricing, or ranking logic.**

---

## ?? HARD BOUNDARIES (LOCKED)

### Pooja Availability Rules:

**Pooja availability is advisory**
- Availability is a signal, not a commitment
- No enforcement of pooja availability
- Subject to change by Pandit

**Final acceptance happens outside availability**
- Acceptance belongs to Module 8
- Availability does not imply acceptance
- Clear separation maintained

**Search may filter, but not decide**
- Search can filter by pooja availability
- Search cannot make booking decisions
- Search is read-only consumption

**?? Pooja availability is advisory - acceptance and booking are separate.**

   - Read-only consumption
   - No editing via dashboards

**?? Pooja availability is consumed read-only - no mutation by consumers.**

# Task 6.8 - Availability Visibility Rules (Public vs Logged-in)

## Overview
This document defines who can see availability information and at what level, without enforcing visibility. This is a **policy and architecture document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. It ensures public users see safe, high-level signals, logged-in users get clearer context, and availability never exposes private schedules.

---

## ?? CRITICAL RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

**This task is VISIBILITY POLICY ONLY.**

? **NO authentication logic**  
? **NO permission enforcement**  
? **NO backend guards**  
? **NO UI rendering rules**  
? **NO tracking or analytics**

If any enforcement or UI logic appears ? REJECT IMMEDIATELY.

---

## ?? PURPOSE (Senior Architect View)

This task exists to define who can see availability information and at what level, without enforcing visibility.

It ensures:
- Public users see safe, high-level signals
- Logged-in users get clearer context
- Availability never exposes private schedules
- Cursor AI does not leak sensitive timing data

This task answers:
**"What availability information is visible - and to whom?"**

---

## ?? VISIBILITY RULES - CONCEPTUAL (LOCKED)

### Availability Visibility Is:

**Role-Based**
- Different information for different roles
- Public users see less detail
- Logged-in users see more detail

**Safe and Privacy-Preserving**
- Never exposes private schedules
- No exact timing for public users
- High-level signals only

**Context-Aware**
- Visibility depends on user role
- Visibility depends on context
- No sensitive data exposure

**?? Availability visibility is role-based and privacy-preserving - not enforcement logic.**

---

## ?? PUBLIC USER VISIBILITY (CONCEPTUAL)

### Public Users (Not Logged In) MAY See:

1. **High-Level Availability Signals**
   - "Available" or "Not Available" indicators
   - General availability status
   - No exact time slots

2. **City/Area Context**
   - Which cities/areas the Pandit serves
   - General service coverage
   - No specific timing

3. **Pooja-Specific Availability Hints**
   - Which poojas the Pandit performs
   - General service types
   - No specific timing

4. **Aggregated Availability Indicators**
   - "Usually available on weekdays"
   - "Available in Mumbai"
   - High-level signals only

**?? Public users see safe, high-level signals - no exact timing or private schedules.**

---

## ?? LOGGED-IN USER VISIBILITY (CONCEPTUAL)

### Logged-In Users (Regular Users) MAY See:

1. **More Detailed Availability Signals**
   - Day-of-week availability
   - Time range hints (e.g., "Morning", "Afternoon")
   - More context than public users

2. **City/Area-Specific Availability**
   - Availability by city/area
   - Service coverage details
   - More specific context

3. **Pooja-Specific Availability Details**
   - Availability by pooja type
   - Service-specific timing hints
   - More detailed context

4. **Availability Status Indicators**
   - "Available this week"
   - "Available next week"
   - More granular signals

**?? Logged-in users see more detailed context - but still no exact private schedules.**

---

## ?? PANDIT VISIBILITY (CONCEPTUAL)

### Pandits (Own Profile) MAY See:

1. **Full Availability Details**
   - All their availability entries
   - Exact time slots
   - All contextual information

2. **Edit Capabilities**
   - Can edit availability
   - Can add/remove entries
   - Full control

3. **Availability History**
   - Past availability entries
   - Update history
   - Full visibility

**?? Pandits see full availability details for their own profile - complete visibility and control.**

---

## ?? ADMIN PANDIT VISIBILITY (CONCEPTUAL)

### Admin Pandit MAY See:

1. **Read-Only Availability View**
   - Can view all Pandits' availability
   - No edit capabilities
   - Dashboard visibility only

2. **Aggregated Availability Data**
   - Availability statistics
   - Coverage analysis
   - Read-only analytics

**?? Admin Pandit sees read-only availability - no edit capabilities.**

---

## ?? SUPER ADMIN VISIBILITY (CONCEPTUAL)

### Super Admin MAY See:

1. **Full Availability Visibility**
   - Can view all Pandits' availability
   - No edit capabilities
   - Dashboard visibility only

2. **System-Wide Availability Data**
   - All availability entries
   - System-wide statistics
   - Governance visibility

**?? Super Admin sees full availability visibility - no edit capabilities, governance only.**

   - Active entries are considered

- **Active vs Inactive:** Inactive entries are ignored, only active entries are considered

**?? Conflict interpretation is semantic only - no enforcement or resolution algorithms.**

# Task 6.11 - Availability Signals for Recommendations (Read-Only)

## Overview
This document defines how availability may be exposed as a passive signal to recommendation systems, without allowing availability to influence ranking, trust, or enforcement. This is a **policy and architecture document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. It ensures availability remains non-authoritative, recommendation systems consume availability only as context, and no ranking or scoring logic leaks into availability.

---

## ?? CRITICAL RULE (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

**This task is SIGNAL EXPOSURE POLICY ONLY.**

? **NO recommendation algorithms**  
? **NO scoring / weighting**  
? **NO ranking logic**  
? **NO machine learning**  
? **NO personalization logic**  
? **NO backend enforcement**

If any recommendation logic appears ? REJECT IMMEDIATELY.

---

## ?? PURPOSE (Senior Architect View)

This task exists to define how availability may be exposed as a passive signal to recommendation systems, without allowing availability to influence ranking, trust, or enforcement.

It ensures:
- Availability remains non-authoritative
- Recommendation systems consume availability only as context
- No ranking or scoring logic leaks into availability
- Cursor AI does not embed availability into recommendation algorithms

This task answers:
**"How may recommendation systems use availability - and where must they stop?"**

---

## ?? SIGNAL EXPOSURE POLICY - CONCEPTUAL (LOCKED)

### Availability as Signal Is:

**Read-Only**
- Recommendation systems read availability data
- No mutations or updates
- No booking logic

**Non-Authoritative**
- Availability is a signal, not a ranking factor
- No scoring or weighting
- No trust implications

**Context-Only**
- Availability provides context
- No decision-making authority
- No enforcement power

**?? Availability as signal is read-only and non-authoritative - not ranking or scoring logic.**

---

## ?? RECOMMENDATION CONSUMPTION RULES (CONCEPTUAL)

### Recommendation Systems MAY:

1. **Read Availability Data**
   - Can query availability entries
   - Can use availability as context
   - Can consume availability signals

2. **Use Availability as Context**
   - Can use availability for context
   - Can show availability status
   - Can use availability for filtering

3. **Display Availability Indicators**
   - Can show "available" or "not available"
   - Can display availability status
   - Can show availability context

4. **Filter by Availability**
   - Can filter recommendations by availability
   - Can use availability as filter criteria
   - Can show availability-based results

5. **Use Availability for Contextual Information**
   - Can use availability for context
   - Can provide availability information
   - Can show availability signals

**?? Recommendation systems consume availability as read-only context - no ranking or scoring.**

---

## ?? DISALLOWED RECOMMENDATION BEHAVIOR

### Recommendation Systems MUST NOT:

? **Rank by Availability**
- No ranking higher based on availability
- No availability-based scoring
- No availability weighting

? **Penalize Low Availability**
- No penalties for less availability
- No negative scoring
- No availability-based demotion

? **Predict Acceptance**
- No prediction of booking acceptance
- No acceptance probability
- No demand inference

? **Combine with Trust or KPIs**
- No combination with trust scores
- No combination with KPIs
- No availability-based trust

? **Infer Demand or Popularity**
- No demand inference
- No popularity scoring
- No availability-based popularity

**?? Availability is opt-in visibility, not performance - no ranking, scoring, or inference.**

# Task 6.12 - Availability Audit & Change History Rules Summary

## Overview
Successfully documented how availability changes are auditable conceptually, without introducing surveillance, enforcement, or penalties. This is a **policy and architecture document only** - no code, no models, no implementation. The document ensures availability changes are traceable if needed, Pandits are not punished for updates, governance has context without micromanagement, and no behavioral control is introduced.

---

**NO CODE** - Audit & Traceability Policy Only

## Document Created

### File: AVAILABILITY_AUDIT_HISTORY_RULES.md

**Purpose:**
- Define why availability audit exists
- Define what high-level change information may be recorded
- Define what audit must never do
- Define hard boundaries preventing surveillance, penalties, or public exposure

---

## Key Definitions

### Audit & Change History - Concept (LOCKED)

**Availability Audit Exists To Record:**
1. When availability was updated
2. That an update occurred
3. The effective state, not every intermediate step

**?? Purpose is traceability, not monitoring - audit is for context, not surveillance.**

---

## Allowed Audit Principles (Conceptual)

**Audit History MAY:**
1. Record timestamp of change
2. Record Pandit identity (self-edit only)
3. Record high-level change type (added / updated / disabled)

**?? Audit history is minimal and high-level - not detailed surveillance or monitoring.**

---

## Disallowed Audit Uses

**Audit MUST NOT:**
- ? Track user demand
- ? Track who viewed availability
- ? Penalize frequent updates
- ? Affect ranking, trust, or visibility
- ? Be exposed publicly

**?? Audit is internal and non-punitive - no surveillance, no penalties, no public exposure.**

---

## Hard Boundaries (LOCKED)

**Audit Must NEVER:**
- ? Track user demand
- ? Track who viewed availability
- ? Penalize frequent updates
- ? Affect ranking, trust, or visibility
- ? Be exposed publicly

**?? Audit is internal - Pandits are not scored on behavior, governance uses audit only for disputes or abuse, no automatic actions are triggered.**

---

## Key Conceptual Distinctions

- **"Audit History" ? "Surveillance"** - Audit history is traceability, surveillance is monitoring
- **"Change Record" ? "Behavioral Tracking"** - Change record is event log, behavioral tracking is monitoring
- **"Traceability" ? "Enforcement"** - Traceability is historical context, enforcement is action
- **"Internal Audit" ? "Public Log"** - Internal audit is governance tool, public log is transparency

**These distinctions prevent confusion with surveillance, monitoring, or behavioral control.**

---

## Why Audit Rules Are Defined Before Implementation

### Architectural Reasons:
1. **Prevent Surveillance Logic** - Clear separation from monitoring
2. **Maintain Non-Punitive Principle** - Audit is not for penalties
3. **Preserve Pandit Autonomy** - Pandits are not monitored
4. **Future-Proof Design** - Audit rules can evolve
5. **Prevent Scope Creep** - Clear boundaries

### Practical Benefits:
- ? No surveillance logic
- ? Non-punitive principle maintained
- ? Pandit autonomy preserved
- ? Future-proof design
- ? Clear boundaries

---

## Audit Principles

1. **Traceability Only** - Audit is for traceability, not monitoring
2. **Non-Punitive** - Audit is not for penalties
3. **Internal Use Only** - Audit is internal, not public
4. **High-Level Only** - Record effective state, not every intermediate step
5. **No Automatic Actions** - No automatic triggers, no enforcement

- **"Encouragement" ? "Enforcement"** - Encouragement is positive reinforcement, enforcement is mandatory action

- ? Clear boundaries

# Task 8.6 Summary - Booking Intent ? Availability Interpretation Rules **Module:** 8 - Booking Intent **Task Type:** NO CODE (Policy & Architecture) **Status:** ? COMPLETE & LOCKED --- ## ?? Task Overview Task 8.6 defines how Booking Intent may reference availability without changing it. This task prevents one of the most common architectural failures: Booking Intent accidentally behaving like a soft booking by "holding" availability. The key principle is that Booking Intent can reference availability conceptually but must never lock, modify, or validate it. --- ## ? Key Deliverables 1. **Interpretation Rules** - **Declarative Reference Only:** Booking Intent may reference user-selected date, time window, and pooja. These are preferences, not constraints. - **No Availability Enforcement:** Booking Intent must NEVER check if Pandit is actually available, validate feasibility against calendar, block other users from sending intents, or reserve/tentatively hold slots. Intent does not compete for time. - **Independence Guarantee:** Multiple Booking Intents MAY exist for the same Pandit, same date/time, or overlapping windows. Concurrency is allowed and expected. 2. **Availability Alignment Guarantees** - **Availability source:** Module 6 only - **Mutability:** Read-only - **Authority:** Never Booking Intent - **Interpretation:** Informational only - **Principle:** Booking Intent reads availability concepts, never availability state 3. **Explicitly Forbidden Behavior (5 Categories)** - Must NEVER reduce visible availability - Must NEVER change availability indicators - Must NEVER affect search results - Must NEVER trigger availability recalculation - Must NEVER cause optimistic locking 4. **Design Principles** - **Interpretation ? Validation:** Reference does not imply validation, preferences do not require feasibility checks - **Reference ? Reservation:** Mentioning availability does not reserve it, no temporal locking occurs - **Signal ? Enforcement:** Intent is informational only, no availability constraints applied - **Intent ? Availability:** Booking Intent and Availability are separate, Module 6 remains authoritative --- ## ?? Architectural Guarantees - **Availability Remains Fully Owned by Module 6:** Booking Intent has no authority over availability - **Read-Only Reference:** Booking Intent reads availability concepts, never availability state - **No Competition for Time:** Intent does not compete for time, multiple intents may coexist - **No Feasibility Checks:** No validation of availability, eligibility, conflicts, or acceptance likelihood - **Module 6 Remains Authoritative:** Availability source, mutability, and authority all remain with Module 6 --- ## ?? Read-Only Consumption **Decision:** Visibility does not enable any actions. Viewing reviews is informational only. **Rationale:** Reviews are immutable and non-authoritative. Visibility should not create dependencies or operational consequences. **Impact:** Reviews remain isolated from operational systems (search, trust, ranking, payments). --- ### 4. Privacy Protection **Decision:** Reviewer identity is protected. Pandits cannot see who wrote reviews. Users cannot see reviewer identity (unless reviewer chooses to display). Only governance has internal access to identity. **Rationale:** Protects reviewer privacy and prevents retaliation or harassment. **Impact:** Safe review environment, encourages honest feedback. --- ### 5. No Authority via Visibility **Decision:** Visibility never implies trust, ranking, validation, eligibility, or operational control. **Rationale:** Prevents architectural contamination where viewing reviews could be misinterpreted as authorization or influence. **Impact:** Reviews remain informational only, no cross-module influence. --- ## ?? 1️⃣ WHY ARE THESE TASKS MARKED “NO CODE” EVEN IN PHASE 2?
This is intentional and correct.
“NO CODE” does NOT mean no backend will ever be written.
🔑 Key distinction (VERY IMPORTANT)
Term
Meaning
Phase 1
Architecture & policy definition (no backend exists yet)
Phase 2
Backend implementation BUT still task-by-task
NO CODE task
A policy-lock task that MUST be written before its implementation task

Why we do this (senior SaaS practice)
For each module, Phase 2 is split into two layers:
🔹 Layer A — Policy / Contract Tasks (NO CODE)
These:
Lock rules
Prevent wrong assumptions
Stop Cursor from inventing logic
Define WHAT code is allowed to do
🔹 Layer B — Implementation Tasks (CODE)
These:
Create models
Write views/services
Enforce rules already locked
📌 You NEVER jump directly to code in complex systems.
If we skip policy tasks:
Cursor invents approval logic
Trust leaks into onboarding
Search/SEO coupling happens
Refactors become inevitable
👉 So “NO CODE” is a guardrail, not a delay.

🚨 When does ACTUAL BACKEND CODE start?
Immediately AFTER policy tasks of the same module.
For Module 2:
Task 2.1 → NO CODE (definition)
Task 2.2 → NO CODE (eligibility rules)
Task 2.3 → 🔜 CODE STARTS HERE (registration flow)
Task 2.4 → CODE (status lifecycle)
Task 2.5+ → CODE where applicable
✅ This is the correct enterprise sequence.

✅ FINAL CURSOR AI PROMPT
(Backend + Database only — NO UI)

You are working on the Nitya Dharma platform.

READ CAREFULLY:
This task is to add FUTURE-READY backend & database support for a News Feed system
by CAPTURING USER BEHAVIOR EVENTS ONLY.

STRICT CONSTRAINTS (NON-NEGOTIABLE):

1. This is BACKEND + DATABASE ONLY.
2. DO NOT build any feed, ranking, sentiment analysis, or personalization.
3. DO NOT change any existing business logic.
4. DO NOT affect Search, Trust, Booking, Reviews, or Governance behavior.
5. DO NOT emit analytics or calculate scores.
6. UI will only trigger events later — not part of this task.
7. All existing Phase-2 and Phase-3 guarantees MUST remain intact.

GOAL:
Capture raw user behavior (like, comment, share, view, click) in a SAFE, IMMUTABLE,
APPEND-ONLY way that can be used in the future to build a news feed engine.

----------------------------------------------------------------
ARCHITECTURE REQUIREMENTS
----------------------------------------------------------------

Use a DUAL-ID STRATEGY (already implemented in project):

- Internal ID: BIGINT (primary key, joins, performance)
- External/Public ID: UUIDv7 (public exposure, URLs, zero enumeration risk)

ALL NEW MODELS MUST:
- Keep BIGINT primary keys
- Add public_id = UUIDv7 (indexed, unique)
- Never expose BIGINT IDs externally

----------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE NEW DJANGO APP
----------------------------------------------------------------

App name: engagement

Add it to INSTALLED_APPS.

----------------------------------------------------------------
DATABASE MODELS (CREATE EXACTLY THESE)
----------------------------------------------------------------

1) UserInteractionEvent  (CORE EVENT LOG — APPEND ONLY)

Model: UserInteractionEvent
Table: engagement_user_interaction_events

Fields:
- id (BIGINT PK)
- public_id (UUIDv7, unique, indexed)
- user (FK → accounts.User, on_delete=CASCADE)
- entity_type (CharField, max_length=50)
- entity_public_id (UUIDv7, indexed)
- interaction_type (CharField, max_length=30)
- metadata (JSONField, nullable)
- created_at (DateTimeField, auto_now_add=True, indexed)

Rules:
- NO updates after insert
- NO deletes
- NO aggregation logic
- Store RAW FACTS ONLY

Allowed interaction_type values (enum or constant list):
- VIEW
- CLICK
- LIKE
- UNLIKE
- SHARE
- COMMENT
- COMMENT_DELETE

Allowed entity_type examples:
- TEMPLE_PAGE
- PAGE_POST
- PANDIT_PROFILE
- REVIEW

----------------------------------------------------------------

2) PostComment (CONTENT, NOT EVENT)

Model: PostComment
Table: engagement_post_comments

Fields:
- id (BIGINT PK)
- public_id (UUIDv7, unique, indexed)
- post_public_id (UUIDv7, indexed)
- user (FK → accounts.User)
- parent_comment (FK → self, null=True, blank=True)
- comment_text (TextField)
- status (CharField, default='active')  # active / hidden / reported
- created_at (DateTimeField)
- updated_at (DateTimeField)

Rules:
- No sentiment analysis
- No moderation logic here
- Governance handled in Module 11

----------------------------------------------------------------

3) PostLike (FAST COUNTER TABLE)

Model: PostLike
Table: engagement_post_likes

Fields:
- id (BIGINT PK)
- post_public_id (UUIDv7, indexed)
- user (FK → accounts.User)
- created_at (DateTimeField)

Constraints:
- UNIQUE (post_public_id, user)

Rules:
- Used ONLY for quick counts
- Each like/unlike MUST ALSO log a UserInteractionEvent

----------------------------------------------------------------
BACKEND SERVICES (NO UI)
----------------------------------------------------------------

Create service layer functions ONLY (no views yet):

- record_view(user, entity_type, entity_public_id, metadata)
- record_click(user, entity_type, entity_public_id, metadata)
- record_like(user, entity_type, entity_public_id)
- record_unlike(user, entity_type, entity_public_id)
- record_share(user, entity_type, entity_public_id, metadata)
- create_comment(user, post_public_id, comment_text)
- delete_comment(user, comment_public_id)
